A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same URoPE work. Their complete main texts and appendices A–C are readable, and the equations, tables, figures, and relocated material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on novel view synthesis, detection and tracking, and stereo depth estimation, together with robustness analyses and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports the retained original experiments plus context-depth and camera-noise experiments and original camera-controlled video examples.

M1.justification: The core lifting, projection, and attention procedure is retained. Section 4.4 adds an optional adaptation that replaces fixed context-view anchors with depths estimated by DepthAnythingV3, while retaining fixed anchors for target views. This differs from v1's existing learned per-layer depth ablation.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds the distinct task of camera-controlled video generation using Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, demonstrated qualitatively. Section 4.4 also adds RealEstate10k scenarios with available context depths and erroneous camera calibration. These substantially broaden task and input-condition coverage; the original datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing comparisons retain their baseline sets. The new camera-noise experiment reuses Plücker Ray and P-RoPE under added test conditions. DepthAnythingV3 supplies depths, Wan supplies the video model, and UCPE is an architectural reference; none is introduced as an evaluated competing baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce estimated context-depth inputs with target depths withheld, camera-parameter corruption under three conditions, and attention-module finetuning of Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B. Existing benchmark protocols and Appendix B training settings are retained. Perturbation magnitudes and detailed video training settings are unspecified.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds two focused analyses: whether available context depths help, and whether performance withstands erroneous focal lengths, rotations, and translations. The latter differs from v1's existing focal-length and context-count distribution shifts. Scaling, head-collapse, anchor-importance, and depth-anchor ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing normalized attention-entropy analysis and its estimation procedure are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched existing numerical results and graphics are unchanged. New Table 6 reports PSNR 26.31 with context depths versus 26.02 without them. New Table 7 reports, for example, PSNR 22.81 for URoPE, 22.17 for P-RoPE, and 22.01 for Plücker Ray under rotation-and-translation noise. Figure A.7 adds video outputs. These are added-condition results, not revised same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the camera-ray and projection definitions, single-view reduction, tensor rearrangement, and computational-complexity argument are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a universal, parameter-free, intrinsics-aware geometric position encoding with coordinate invariance, kernel compatibility, and benefits across the original tasks. The added experiments support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that externally supplied context depths can improve performance and that URoPE tolerates noisy camera parameters. Existing explanations of anchor specialization and head collapse are retained. The conclusion and Appendix C still identify dependence on available camera calibration as a limitation.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a project-website notice into an explicit statement of code availability. New passages identify DepthAnythingV3 as the depth source and Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B attention finetuning for video generation. Existing Appendix B implementation recipes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to pixelSplat, Wan, and UCPE, and uses the already cited DepthAnythingV3 as an experimental depth source. The main positioning against ray encodings, GTA, P-RoPE, and RayRoPE remains unchanged. Reference renumbering and publication-metadata updates do not change that positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized prose and caption edits, standardized P-RoPE terminology, an internship footnote, and an added appendix subsection for video generation. Most paragraphs and the overall section organization are retained; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 7 and the two-panel video Figure A.7. Table 5 is compacted beside Table 6, and existing tables and appendix figures are relocated or renumbered. Existing graphical content is retained, with limited caption, header, spacing, and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Tables 6 and 7 add useful evidence about exploiting context depth and tolerating calibration errors, questions left untested in v1. The code-availability statement also improves access information while prior results remain intact. The gains are limited: noise magnitudes are unspecified, and the new video application has only qualitative examples without quantitative evaluation or a detailed training recipe.
